Etienne and Louise LaMarque's historic home in Old Mines, Missouri, constructed in 1818 and acquired by LaMarque in 1822, stands near St. Joachim Catholic Church, built in 1831 with their significant donations. This colonial French-style residence remains privately occupied. (See: Paul T. Hellmann, 2005, Historical Gazetteer of the United States, p.635; Vallé Higginbotham, 1968, John Smith T, Missouri Pioneer, p.18.)

The 1934 U.S. postage stamp commemorating Wisconsin's tercentenary, depicting Jean Nicolet's landing at the Bay of Green Bay in 1634. Public domain image via Wikimedia Commons.

Page from The discovery and conquests of the Northwest, featuring “Fort Wayne in 1795.” Published in 1880 by Rufus Blanchard and Elijah Middlebrook Haines. Digitized by The Library of Congress, sponsored by the Sloan Foundation. Public domain image via Wikimedia Commons.

Photograph of the Solomon Juneau statue in Milwaukee, circa 1890. Solomon Juneau, a French-Canadian fur trader, is recognized as Milwaukee's founder and first mayor. The city's modern history began in 1795 when fur trader Jacques Vieau established a post, later transferred to Juneau in 1818, making him the city's first permanent white resident and founder. Public domain image via Wikimedia Commons.

A sketch of Grand Rapids in 1831, showing the Baptist mission on the west side of the river and Louis Campau's trading post at the center right. Louis Campau, a fur trader and founder of Grand Rapids, established the post, which spurred the area's early development. Public domain image via Wikimedia Commons.

Photograph of the Fort St. Joseph monument, rear view, with a man standing to the right. Taken on December 19, 1920. Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument, LIBI_00312_13377. Unknown photographer.

The historical marker at Fort Ouiatenon in Tippecanoe County, Indiana, photographed on January 28, 2007. The marker details the fort's establishment in 1717 by French Canada, its role in countering British expansion, and its eventual destruction by American soldiers in 1791. Public domain image via Wikimedia Commons.
